8
A car is travelling at constant velocity. At time t = 0, the driver of the car sees an obstacle in the
road and then brakes to a halt. The graph shows the variation with t of the velocity of the car.
velocity / m s–1
20
0
0
0.8
5.0
t / s
How far does the car travel in the 5.0 s after the driver sees the obstacle?
A
16 m
B
42 m
C
58 m
D
84 m

hints: Notice the graph stays flat at $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ from $t = 0$ to $t = 0.8 \text{ s}$, then falls linearly to zero at $t = 5.0 \text{ s}$.
Recall distance is the area under a velocity-time graph, so split this shape into a rectangle for thinking time plus a triangle for braking.
Calculate $20 \times 0.8$ for the first part and $0.5 \times 20 \times (5.0-0.8)$ for the second part, then add them.
walkthrough: Identify the two motions: constant $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ from 0 to 0.8 s while reacting, then uniform deceleration from 0.8 s to 5.0 s to rest.
Use distance = area under velocity-time graph. The total area is a rectangle plus a triangle.
Thinking distance = area of rectangle $= v \times t = 20 \times 0.8 = 16 \text{ m}$.
Braking time $= 5.0 - 0.8 = 4.2 \text{ s}$. Braking distance = area of triangle $= 0.5 \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = 0.5 \times 4.2 \times 20 = 42 \text{ m}$.
Total distance $= 16 + 42 = 58 \text{ m}$ with unit $\text{m}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is only the $20 \times 0.8 = 16 \text{ m}$ rectangle for the 0 to 0.8 s thinking time, not the total 5.0 s distance.

B.explanation: This is only the braking triangle $0.5 \times 20 \times 4.2 = 42 \text{ m}$, missing the 16 m travelled before braking starts.

C.explanation: Total area under the velocity-time graph is $16 \text{ m} + 42 \text{ m} = 58 \text{ m}$ for 0 to 5.0 s.

D.explanation: This uses $20 \times 4.2 = 84 \text{ m}$, treating the braking time at full $20 \text{ m s}^{-1}$ instead of the decreasing velocity triangle.
